# Transcripts and PhraseFind AI (8.2)

Editing Guide ch.14, "PhraseFind AI" (p.436-453), with the 2026.8 guide's additions (p.446-447, p.451-452, p.455-456).
8.2 is in five parts (docs/ROADMAP.md): 8.2a transcripts and the engine, 8.2b the Transcript Tool, 8.2c PhraseFind AI
in the Find window, 8.2d transcripts out, 8.2e AutoCut. This page covers what is built.

## Transcripts (8.2a)

* "Transcripts are generated by analyzing and indexing all audible dialog for individual clips" (p.442). A transcript
  (`model::Transcript`) is a master clip's words, each with its start and end in seconds from the clip's first frame,
  in lines with a Speaker ID each ("Speaker 1", "Speaker 2" ... until named, p.444-445).
* "Only master clips are transcribed" (p.448): master clips with sound, audio-only ones too. Subclips, groups and
  sequences will reference their master clips' transcripts (8.2b).
* "Media Composer preserves the original transcript generated when the clip was transcribed. Edited transcripts are
  stored separately" (2026.8 guide p.447): `Transcript::original` holds the lines as transcribed once they are edited.
* The store (`model::TranscriptStore`): "Transcripts for clips that have already been transcribed are available for use
  across multiple projects" (p.442) and are "stored in a central database for projects on your system" (p.453). Ours:
  one JSON file per clip, named by its MobID, in the user's application data folder's `Transcripts`
  (`LUMENIS_TRANSCRIPTS` for tests; every ctest has its own).

## The engine (8.2a)

* "PhraseFind AI does not require an Internet connection. All processing is done on your local system" (p.436). The
  engine is an `ext::TranscriptionProvider`; built in is whisper.cpp's `whisper-cli` (MIT) with a ggml model
  (`media::WhisperProvider`, BUILDING.md "Transcripts"). It is run once per clip on a 16 kHz mono WAV file of the
  clip's first audio track, asked for one word per segment (`-ml 1 -sow`) as JSON (`-oj`), and reports its progress
  (`-pp`).
* Speaker IDs: with a tinydiarize model (`-tdrz`, "tdrz" in the model's file name) whisper.cpp marks speaker turns.
  Ours (`model::transcriptLines`): a turn goes back to the speaker before, or to a new Speaker ID after the first,
  which suits a conversation of two; the user corrects the rest (8.2b). Without turns every line is Speaker 1.
* Lines (ours): a line ends at a speaker turn, at a pause of more than 2 seconds, and at the end of a sentence once it
  lasts 30 seconds (the 2026.8 New Line After default, 2026.8 guide p.446).
* The Language Hint (p.448) is passed as whisper.cpp's `-l`; Multilingual is `auto`.

## Which bins are transcribed (8.2a)

* Bin > Include Bin in Transcription and Exclude Bin from Transcription, also on a bin's right-click menu in the Sidebar
  (p.447; `MainWindow::setBinsTranscribed`). They act on the Sidebar's selected bins, else the active bin.
* "Text is displayed to the right of a bin, in the Bin Container sidebar, to indicate if it is set to Transcription On or
  Transcription Off" (p.447): the Sidebar's third column (`BinTreeModel::kTranscriptionColumn`).
* The status is kept in the project folder's `Transcription.json`, by the bins' node ids, not in the bins: "When
  copying or moving bins on the macOS Finder or Windows Explorer level, the status of transcription will not be moved
  with it" (p.447). A bin not listed is included.

## Background transcription (8.2a)

* "By default, Media Composer will create a transcription for all media in a project" (p.446): every master clip with
  sound in an included bin without a transcript is transcribed, one Background Queue job per clip at Low priority
  (`MainWindow::queueTranscriptions`). Failures go to the Console.
* "Pause background transcription while editing" (p.447, on by default): ours checks every two seconds and queues new
  clips only once there has been no key press, click or wheel turn for ten seconds ("After ten seconds of inactivity,
  the transcription process will continue again", p.448). A clip being transcribed finishes.

## The Transcript Project setting (8.2a)

File > Settings > Project > Transcript (p.447-450):

* Include all new bins in transcription (on): off, a new bin starts excluded (`BinContainer::binCreated`).
* Pause background transcription while editing (on).
* Language Hint: Multilingual (the default) or a language. Ours lists whisper.cpp's well-supported languages; the guide
  says "21 languages are supported" (p.441) without naming them. The New Project tab has it too, "beneath options for
  Transcription" (p.448): the choice is written into the new project's Settings.json as its Transcript setting; "If
  Transcript settings have already been added to the Site settings for a particular workstation, these options will be
  grayed out" (`SelectProjectDialog`, 8.2b2b).
* Subclips/Groups: Ask (the default), Use Master Clips Transcripts, Transcribe Subclip or Group (p.449-450); used from
  8.2b on.
* Manage Speakers (p.445, 8.2b2b), a "button" option (`SettingsDialog::buttonClicked`, `toolRequested`), opens Manage
  Speaker Names; Manage Transcripts (p.453, 8.2d) opens Manage Transcripts.

## The Transcript Tool (8.2b1)

Tools > Transcript Tool (p.442; command `tools.transcript_tool`) opens it as the "Transcript" panel
(`ui::TranscriptTool`, wired in `main_window_transcripts.cpp`).

* What it shows (`model::shownTranscript`): "the Transcript Tool will always reference master clip transcripts"
  (p.449). A master clip shows its own; a subclip its master clip's from where it starts (its Clip source's offset); a
  group its selected angle's; a sequence or multigroup "the transcript for the master clip associated with any selected
  audio tracks" (p.449), each segment's words placed at its frames. A clip on two tracks is shown once.
* "the Transcript Tool will update each time a clip is loaded into the Source monitor, or a sequence is loaded into the
  Record monitor" (p.442): the side follows the last load; the Source/Record button switches it ("green when the Source
  side is selected", p.444).
* Each line: its timecode (Show Timecode), its speaker (Show Speaker ID) and its words.
* "ganged to the Source or Record monitor's playhead, which displays as a bold, green (for Source) or blue (for Record)
  word" (p.442); the word is the last one starting at or before the position.
* "Clicking on a word in a transcript will also move the playhead ... selecting text in the Transcript Tool will set In
  and Out marks" (p.442): IN at the first word's frame, OUT on the last word's last frame. Shift+Left/Right move the end
  of the selection word by word. Marks set in the monitor select their words. Unganged (the gang button), neither
  follows the other (p.444).
* Copy: the selected text, plain (p.442).
* Search (p.444): every place the typed words follow one another, ignoring case and punctuation (ours, as PhraseFind,
  p.441); the arrows and Enter go to the next or previous match after the playhead word, going round.
* The track button for sequences, groups and multigroups (p.449): the audio tracks whose transcripts are shown, all of
  them until chosen.
* Fast menu (p.443): Show Timecode, Show Speaker ID, Show Not Transcribed, Set Font, Transcribe Remaining Clips.
  "Clip not transcribed" with a Transcribe button; transcribing from the tool runs the clips at High priority on the
  Background Queue, ahead of background transcription (`MainWindow::transcribeNow`). Ours: Transcribe also works for
  clips in excluded bins.
* Editing with V and B from the tool's marks works through the monitors.

## Editing transcripts (8.2b2a)

Changes go into the clip's transcript in the store (`model::editWords` and friends in `transcript.h`, through
`TranscriptTool::editRequested` and `MainWindow::editTranscript`). The first change keeps the transcribed lines
(`Transcript::original`, 2026.8 guide p.447). Ours: transcript changes are not undo steps; Revert is the way back.

* Text (p.445-446): double-click a word, or the selected words, to edit them in place; right-click > Edit Text. "Only
  one sentence can be edited at a time": one transcript line. "How Timing is Preserved": a single word keeps its timing;
  several words in one word's space share it evenly; otherwise unchanged words are found (ours: the longest common
  sequence of words, ignoring case and punctuation) and keep their times, the words between two of them sharing the time
  of the old words between (or, with none, of the kept word before). Removing every word of a line removes it.
* "The right-click menu now displays only Edit Text and Copy when text is selected" (p.446); on a word without a
  selection: Edit Text, Start New Line, Revert (2026.8 guide p.447).
* Find and Replace (fast menu, p.446): every place the found words follow one another in a line, ignoring case and
  punctuation, in every shown clip's transcript. Ours: the replacement's own punctuation is used.
* Speaker IDs (p.444-445): double-click a speaker's name to rename it ("All instance of that speaker name in the
  transcript are immediately renamed"). Right-click it: Identify Speaker (the names known, Clear Name, Rename) and
  Correct Speaker ID (the transcript's speakers, Add New Speaker "in this one instance"). Ours: Identify Speaker with a
  new name names the line's speaker when it speaks only there, else gives the line a new Speaker ID with that name.
* Improving Transcript Readability (2026.8 guide p.446): Group Speaker Lines shows consecutive lines of one speaker as a
  paragraph, broken again after New Line After seconds (30 by default; `model::groupedLines`). Ours: both are the
  tool's, not kept between sessions.
* Start New Line splits a line before the word; Revert puts back the original lines in a line's time; Revert Transcript
  (fast menu) every shown clip's transcript (2026.8 guide p.447).

## Manage Speaker Names (8.2b2b)

The Transcript setting's Manage Speakers button opens it (p.445; `src/ui/speaker_names_dialog.*`,
`MainWindow::manageSpeakers`):

* "a list of all available speakers that have been added or edited in transcripts for your current project": the
  project's own list (`model::ProjectSpeakers`, `<project>/Speakers.json`) with the names given in the transcripts of the
  project's master clips. A name in no transcript is dimmed.
* Double-click renames a name in every transcript of the project (`model::renameSpeakerName`; to a name a transcript
  already has, the two speakers merge) and in the list.
* "+" adds a name to the list, "added in advance ... to select from a list of available names" (ours: it starts as "New
  Speaker", edited in place). Identify Speaker offers the list's names and the transcripts' (`MainWindow::projectSpeakerNames`
  into `TranscriptTool::setKnownSpeakers`).
* Merge, with several names selected, makes them "a single Speaker ID" in each transcript (`model::mergeSpeakerNames`;
  ours: named as the first selected, the lowest of the IDs).
* Clear/Delete: "Delete" for dimmed names removes them from the list; "Clear" for used names "will remove that name from
  all transcripts in this project" (`model::clearSpeakerName`; the speakers show as "Speaker n" again). Ours: with a mix
  selected the button reads Clear and each name gets its own; a cleared name that was in the list stays there, dimmed.
* Every change applies at once (`MainWindow::applySpeakerNameChange`); Done closes the window. It is window modal over
  the setting's dialog.

## PhraseFind AI (8.2c)

The Find window's PhraseFind AI button on the Clips and Sequences tab (p.436-441; `src/model/phrase_find.*`,
`FindWindow::phraseFind`, `MainWindow::connectPhraseFind`):

* "PhraseFind AI indexes and finds audio in master clips, subclips and group clips. Only your project needs to be
  opened, and you do not need to have the bins open": the bins of the search scope (the project's, or Current Bin),
  open or not, and their master clips (audio-only too), subclips and groups (not multigroups). Our index is the
  transcripts: each clip's words as it shows them (`model::shownTranscript`), so a subclip finds what is said within it,
  a group what its selected angle says.
* "case insensitive and ignores punctuation" (p.441, `model::phraseWords`).
* Score, "ranging from 100 to 50 ... the score with the higher value is more probable" (p.438). Ours: 100 where the
  words come in order (across lines too); 50 to 90 for a line holding at least half of them in any order, a word that
  only begins with one of three or more letters counting half. Results best first, then in bin order; one row for each
  place.
* "The Score and Transcription columns always display in PhraseFind AI" after Name and Bin (p.439); Transcription is
  the line (or lines) the words are in. Select Columns adds the rest as for text find. The filters also take Score and
  Transcription; Any Column looks in the Transcription and the item's columns.
* Load into monitor: "places the blue position bar on the frame immediately before the dialogue starts. A Mark IN point
  displays on the frame immediately preceding the audio dialogue, the bin opens and the clip highlights inside the bin"
  (p.437; `model::phraseMarkIn`). Without Load into monitor the bin opens with the clip selected, as text find does.
* The PhraseFind AI Index (p.437, p.441): green as far as the master clips with sound in the bins included in
  transcription have transcripts (`MainWindow::phraseIndexStatus`), read every two seconds while the window shows; full
  with nothing to transcribe. "Found" counts the results.
* The Settings button (p.441): Stop/Start PhraseFind AI Indexing stops or starts background transcription
  (`MainWindow::setTranscriptionIndexing`; Transcribe still works); the Search Data Directory is shown, dimmed, as the
  store's folder (`LUMENIS_TRANSCRIPTS`); Manage Transcripts opens Manage Transcripts (8.2d).
* Ours: no Cancel button, the search over transcripts being quick; filtering applies when the search runs.

## Transcripts out (8.2d)

`src/model/transcript_export.*`, `src/ui/transcript_dialogs.*` and `main_window_transcripts.cpp`:

* The bin's right-click Transcript menu (p.450-453, 2026.8 guide p.456): Export Transcript and Share Transcripts for clips
  and sequences, Delete Transcript for clips (master clips, subclips, groups: the master clip's, a group's selected
  angle's), Export SubCap for sequences. The Timeline's right-click Transcript > Create SubCap (p.452). Commands
  `bin.export_transcript`, `bin.share_transcripts`, `bin.delete_transcript`, `bin.export_subcap`,
  `timeline.create_subcap`.
* The Transcribe window (`TranscribeTracksDialog`): "select the audio tracks from your sequence" for a sequence's Export
  Transcript, Export SubCap and Create SubCap, with "Use Marks" and "Limit characters per caption" for captions
  (p.452-453). Ours: every audio track checked at first, a 32-character limit offered when turned on.
* Export Transcript (p.450): "a text file (.txt), containing timecode and unique speaker ID information ... can also be
  imported back ... for use in the SubCap effect". Ours is an Avid DS caption file (`model::exportedTranscriptText`):
  each line a caption from its first word to its last word's end, its first row the speaker ("Speaker 1:"), so the
  SubCap effect's Import Caption Data reads it as it is. Several items go into a chosen folder, a file each.
* Captions (`model::transcriptCaptions`): a line a caption; with the limit, rows broken between words, two rows to a
  caption (ours); each ending before the next starts; with Use Marks, only between the Record monitor's IN and OUT.
  Export SubCap writes Avid DS (.txt) or EBU N19 (.stl) as the SubCap effect's Export Caption Data does. Create SubCap
  adds a video track above the others with a SubCap effect over the captions, subdivided at them
  (`model::createSubCapTrack`), as one undo step.
* Share Transcripts (p.451): the selection's transcripts in one file with the project's Language Hint. Avid's .avt is
  undocumented, so ours is JSON, "cutthulhu-transcripts" with the suffix `.cttr` (`model::writeSharedTranscripts`).
  Importing needs the same Language Hint ("Project Transcript Language Hint settings need to match when exporting and
  importing"). Peer-to-peer sharing is below (8.7b).
* Delete Transcript also on the Transcript Tool's fast menu (2026.8 guide p.456: "The currently loaded transcript is
  immediately deleted"): every transcript it shows.
* Manage Transcripts (2026.8 guide p.455-456), from Script > Manage Transcripts, the Find window's Settings and the
  Transcript setting's button (`ManageTranscriptsDialog`, `MainWindow::manageTranscripts`): "Select the project whose
  transcripts you want to delete and click Delete ... Click Import". Ours: our store is not kept by project, so the
  window lists the current project's transcribed clips (clip, language, created, edited); Delete removes the selected
  ones, Import reads a shared transcripts file, Export shares them all (p.451: "transcripts for an entire project can be
  exported using the Manage Transcripts window"), Done closes it.

## Peer-to-peer transcript sharing (8.7b)

"Media Composer also supports shared transcript databases across workstations via Avid NEXIS ... Access to this
functionality requires Avid NEXIS to be enabled" (p.451). Ours: any folder on shared storage, as bin locking finds it
(`model::isSharedLocation`, `LUMENIS_SHARED_BINS`).

* "Host Shared Transcripts: Allows the current workstation's database to be accessed by other workstations. Use Shared
  Transcripts: References the database on the host workstation" (p.452). The guide does not say where these are; ours:
  the Transcript setting's Transcript Sharing menu (Off, Host Shared Transcripts, Use Shared Transcripts) and Shared
  Transcripts Folder (settings.json, applied by `MainWindow::applyTranscriptSharing`). Hosting copies this
  workstation's transcripts into the folder and names this station as the host there (`model::hostTranscripts`,
  `Host.json`); Use reads and writes the folder the host shares. A folder off shared storage, or none, leaves sharing
  off with a line in the Console.
* "When transcript sharing is enabled, all transcript functionality reads and writes to the hosting workstation's
  database. New transcripts are added to the shared database, allowing multiple stations to process media
  transcriptions simultaneously" (p.452): `model::setTranscriptSharing` makes the shared folder every
  `TranscriptStore`'s default (`TranscriptStore::localFolder` stays this station's own). A station transcribing a clip
  holds its entry's lock, so other stations skip that clip (`MainWindow::queueTranscription`).
* "Transcript entries lock when users are writing or editing them. If a conflict occurs, users are prompted and can
  choose to abort on the other station and obtain the lock" (p.452): a `<clip>.lock` file beside the entry with the
  station (`model::transcriptStation`, `LUMENIS_STATION` for tests) and the time (`TranscriptStore::lockOf`/`lock`/
  `unlock`). A save takes the lock while it writes and fails while another station holds it; `MainWindow::editTranscript`
  holds it through an edit and `saveTranscript` asks the question ("Transcript Locked", Yes takes the lock over;
  `setTranscriptTakeOverHook` for tests). The other station's next write then fails and says so in its Console.
* "Deleting a transcript removes it for all users sharing the database" (p.452): Delete removes the entry and its lock
  from the shared folder.
* "Hosting does not require Media Composer to be running on the host station, but if the host is offline or the search
  database is stopped, transcripts will not be available" (p.452): the folder is read wherever it is; when it cannot be
  reached there are no transcripts, and the Console says so (`model::sharedTranscriptsReachable`).
* "Media Composer transcripts are tied to master clips" and "Only users with access to the relevant shared projects and
  media can view or edit associated transcripts" (p.452) hold as they are: entries are found by the clips' MobIDs.

## AutoCut (8.2e)

"Creating a Multicamera Edit Using Transcript Data" (2026.8 guide p.451-452):

* "Assign each identified speaker to a corresponding camera angle": the guide says it is done in the Transcript Tool
  without saying how. Ours: with a group in the Source monitor, a speaker's right-click menu has Assign to Camera Angle,
  listing None and the group's angles (`TranscriptTool::setCameraAngles`, `speakerAngleChosen`,
  `MainWindow::assignSpeakerAngle`). The assignment is kept in the group, by speaker name as the transcript shows it
  (`GroupClip::speakerAngles`).
* "Select a group clip segment using the Segment tool. Right-click the segment. Select AutoCut": the Timeline's
  right-click AutoCut (`timeline.autocut`), enabled with a group segment selected. `model::autoCut` switches the
  segment's angle at the first word of each line inside it whose speaker has an angle (`setGroupAngleAt` with a cut),
  as one undo step for every selected segment (`MainWindow::autoCut`). "AutoCut applies only to the selected group clip
  segment"; "If a speaker is not assigned to a camera angle, no automatic switch is applied": frames before the first
  switch, and a line of an unassigned speaker, keep the angle they have.
* Ours: the transcript is the one the group shows (its selected angle's master clip, as the Transcript Tool's); only the
  video tracks' group segments are switched, the sound staying as patched.

## Tests

* `tst_transcript`: lines from engine words, JSON round trips, the store, the bins' status.
* `tst_transcription`: whisper-cli's JSON, a linked clip transcribed through a stand-in engine, `WhisperProvider` running
  a stand-in `whisper-cli` script (not on Windows).
* `tst_transcript editing`, `groupedSpeakerLines`: timing kept through edits, Find and Replace, speakers, Start New
  Line, Revert; `tst_transcripts_ui transcriptTool` the same through the tool.
* `tst_group_clip autoCutFromSpeakers` and scenario `48-autocut.json`: the speakers' angles kept in the group, the
  switches; `tst_transcripts_ui autoCutFromTranscript` Assign to Camera Angle and the Timeline's AutoCut.
* `tst_transcript peerToPeerSharing`: hosting, locks between stations and the take-over, the shared folder as the store's
  default, an unreachable host, deletes; `tst_transcripts_ui peerToPeerSharing` the Transcript setting's sharing, the
  take-over question, storage that is not shared.
* `tst_transcript transcriptsOut`: the exported text read back as captions, captions with a limit and marks, Create
  SubCap's track, the shared file; `tst_transcripts_ui transcriptsOut` the bin's Transcript menu, Export Transcript,
  Share and Import with the Language Hint check, Delete, Export SubCap and Create SubCap on a sequence, Manage
  Transcripts.
* `tst_transcript phraseFind`: scores, order, subclips, filters; `tst_transcripts_ui phraseFindWindow` the Find window's
  button, columns, index status, loading with the IN mark, Stop/Start indexing.
* `tst_transcript speakerNames`: rename, merge and clear by name, the project's list; `tst_transcripts_ui
  manageSpeakerNames` the window and the setting's button; `tst_select_project_dialog languageHintGoesIntoTheProject`.
* `tst_transcript shownTranscripts`: what a clip, subclip, group and sequence show; `tst_transcripts_ui transcriptTool`:
  the tool in the application (sides, clicks, selections, search, a sequence, Transcribe).
* `tst_transcripts_ui`: Include/Exclude Bin in Transcription with the Sidebar's status, queuing the included bins' clips
  once, the Language Hint reaching the engine, new bins excluded.
